parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish ervage, erbaje, erbage, herbaje, herbage (c. 1250), from Old French erbage, from Early Medieval Latin herbāticum, from Latin herba (“grass”). By surface analysis, hierba + -aje. Doublet of herbazgo.
Borrowed from Old French mareschal, from Early Medieval Latin mariscalcus, from Frankish *marhaskalk (“equerry”), from *marh (“horse”) + *skalk (“servant”), from Proto-Germanic *marhaz + *skalkaz.
